fields.TOPIC: Responsibility for validation + acceptance of pseudonyms
fields.CONTENT: Relying parties shall be RESPONSIBLE for carrying out the authentication and validation of the person identification data (PID) and electronic attestations of attributes (EAA) requested from the European Digital Identity Wallet. Relying parties SHALL NOT refuse the use of PSEUDONYMS where the identification of the user is not required by Union or national law.
fields.PURPOSE: Places the verification duty squarely on the relying party and at the same time protects the right to use pseudonyms under Article 5 against being undermined in practice.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(4) · The seven user functionalities Describes, from the user's perspective, what the European Digital Identity Wallet must be able to do: (a) securely request, store, delete and selectively present attributes, (b) generate pseudonyms and store them encrypted and locally, (c) interact with another person's European Digital Identity Wallet, (d) a dashboard with a complete transaction history, including erasure requests and a button for reporting to the data protection authority, (e) sign by means of qualified electronic signatures and seal by means of qualified electronic seals, (f) download data, (g) exercise data portability. Together with paragraphs 5, 8 and 14, this paragraph forms the subject matter of certification under Article 5c(1). Article 5 eIDAS · Use of pseudonyms A single, unnumbered sentence: without prejudice to specific identification obligations and to the legal effect given to pseudonyms under national law, the use of pseudonyms chosen by the user shall not be prohibited in electronic transactions. The Article has NO paragraphs. It is given concrete form in Article 5a(4), point (b), Article 5b(9) and Article 32(1), point (e). Relevance here: the second sentence of paragraph 9 makes the general right to use pseudonyms enforceable against the relying party. Article 32 eIDAS · Requirements for the validation of qualified electronic signatures Sets out in eight points when a validation may confirm validity: a qualified certificate complying with Annex I at the time of signing, issuance by a qualified trust service provider and validity at that time, correspondence of the validation data, correct provision of the data representing the signatory, clear indication where a pseudonym is used, creation by a qualified electronic signature creation device, integrity of the data, and compliance with Article 26. Paragraph 2 additionally requires that the result be displayed in an understandable way.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Does the service accept pseudonyms wherever there is no legal obligation to identify the user by real name?
fields.KEY POINT: Only a party that can name a legal basis for doing so may refuse a pseudonym.

fields.ADDRESSEE: Intermediaries acting on behalf of relying parties
fields.CONTENT: Intermediaries acting on behalf of relying parties SHALL BE DEEMED TO BE relying parties and shall store NO data about the CONTENT of the transaction.
fields.PURPOSE: Prevents an unregulated intermediate data layer from forming between the European Digital Identity Wallet and the service.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5b(1) · Obligation to register Requires anyone intending to rely upon European Digital Identity Wallets for the provision of public or private services to register in the Member State in which it is established. Only registered entities can be authenticated by the European Digital Identity Wallet. Article 5a(16) · Unlinkability in the technical framework Point (a) prohibits providers of electronic attestations of attributes or any other party from obtaining, after issuance of the attestation, data that would allow transactions or user behaviour to be tracked, linked or correlated. Point (b) requires techniques which ensure unlinkability where the attestation of attributes does not require the identification of the user. Whereas paragraph 5, point (b) prohibits the issuer from being informed of use, paragraph 16 prohibits the bringing together of data – technically this leads to techniques such as selective disclosure and zero-knowledge proofs.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is an identity broker in use? Does it store transaction content?
fields.KEY POINT: Deemed a relying party – and yet may store no transaction content.

fields.CONTENT: The Commission shall establish technical specifications and procedures for the requirements referred to in paragraphs 2, 5 and 6 to 9, within the framework of the European Digital Identity Wallet implementing act referred to in Article 5a(23).
fields.PURPOSE: Without a uniform format, the registration of relying parties is neither machine-readable nor usable across borders.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(23) · Implementing act on the core European Digital Identity Wallet requirements In practice the most important empowering provision of the Regulation. The Commission establishes reference standards, specifications and procedures for paragraphs 4, 5, 8 and 18 – this is the legal basis of the Architecture and Reference Framework. It is at the same time one of the two triggers of the 24-month deadline in paragraph 1. Numerous further provisions (5b(11), 5d(7), 5e(5), 45d(5), 45e(2), 45f(6) and (7)) expressly require alignment with that act. “the Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, establish a list of reference standards and, where necessary, establish specifications and procedures for the requirements referred to in paragraphs 4, 5, 8 and 18 of this Article” ✓ Article 5a(23) eIDAS Article 48(2) eIDAS · Examination procedure Refers to Article 5 of the Comitology Regulation (EU) No 182/2011. A committee composed of representatives of the Member States delivers an opinion by qualified majority; where the opinion is negative, the Commission may not adopt the draft. All implementing acts under this Regulation follow this procedure.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Has the implementing act been adopted, and does it cover paragraphs 2, 5 and 6-9?
fields.KEY POINT: Not paragraphs 1, 3, 4, 10 – the implementing act covers only 2, 5 and 6-9.

fields.CONTENT: The conformity of the European Digital Identity Wallet AND of the electronic identification scheme under which it is provided with Article 5a PARAGRAPHS 4, 5 and 8, with the requirement of LOGICAL SEPARATION laid down in Article 5a(14) and, where applicable, with the standards referred to in Article 5a(24) shall be certified by conformity assessment bodies DESIGNATED by the Member States (MS).
fields.PURPOSE: Defines exactly and exhaustively what is certified – everything else in Article 5a is a matter for supervision, not for certification.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(4) · The seven user functionalities Describes, from the user's perspective, what the European Digital Identity Wallet must be able to do: (a) securely request, store, delete and selectively present attributes, (b) generate pseudonyms and store them encrypted and locally, (c) interact with another person's European Digital Identity Wallet, (d) a dashboard with a complete transaction history, including erasure requests and a button for reporting to the data protection authority, (e) sign by means of qualified electronic signatures and seal by means of qualified electronic seals, (f) download data, (g) exercise data portability. Together with paragraphs 5, 8 and 14, this paragraph forms the subject matter of certification under Article 5c(1). Article 5a(5) · Mandatory technical characteristics The inside view of paragraph 4. Point (a) lists eleven interfaces (issuance, request, presentation, user interaction, onboarding, European Digital Identity Wallet-to-European Digital Identity Wallet, relying party authentication, verification of authenticity, erasure requests, reporting to the authority, creation of qualified electronic signatures) – in effect the table of contents of the ARF. Point (b) prohibits any feedback to the issuer of the electronic attestation of attributes, point (d) mandates assurance level high, and point (g) the free-of-charge qualified electronic signature for natural persons. Article 5a(8) · Free-of-charge validation mechanisms Requires the Member State to provide two free-of-charge verification paths running in opposite directions: point (a) allows verification of whether a European Digital Identity Wallet presented is authentic and valid; point (b) allows the user to verify whether the requesting relying party is registered and genuine. Without this two-way verifiability, Article 5b(8) (self-identification of the relying party) could not be verified. Forms part of the subject matter of certification under Article 5c(1). Article 5a(14) · User control and logical separation Prohibits the provider of the European Digital Identity Wallet from collecting information about use that is not necessary, and from combining European Digital Identity Wallet data with data from other services of its own or of third parties. It must also keep the data logically separate from all other holdings. Where the European Digital Identity Wallet is provided by private parties under paragraph 2, point (b) or (c), Article 45h(3) (functional separation) applies mutatis mutandis in addition. This is the only paragraph outside 4, 5 and 8 that is expressly certified. “Personal data relating to the provision of the European Digital Identity Wallet shall be kept logically separate from any other data held by the provider of the European Digital Identity Wallet” ✓ Article 5a(14) eIDAS Relevance here: the only paragraph outside 4, 5 and 8 that is expressly included in the scope of certification. Article 5a(24) · Implementing act on user onboarding Empowers the Commission to establish reference standards and procedures for the onboarding of users – either by electronic identification means conforming to assurance level high, or by means conforming to assurance level substantial in conjunction with additional remote onboarding procedures that together meet the requirements of assurance level high. Without this route, citizens without an assurance-level-high identity document could not get into the European Digital Identity Wallet. Article 5d · Publication of the list of certified European Digital Identity Wallets Requires the Member States to notify the Commission and the Cooperation Group without delay of both certified and withdrawn wallets, and states the minimum content of that notification. The Commission maintains a machine-readable list published in the Official Journal and incorporates changes within one month. The list of wallets is to be distinguished from the trusted list of trust service providers under Article 22.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Does the certificate submitted cover exactly 5a(4), (5), (8), (14) and, where applicable, (24)?
fields.KEY POINT: Scope of certification: 4 – 5 – 8 – 14 (+24). Learn this sequence of numbers by heart.

fields.CONTENT: In so far as requirements are relevant for CYBERSECURITY, certification shall be carried out in accordance with the European cybersecurity certification schemes adopted pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2019/881 (Cybersecurity Act) and referred to in the implementing act under paragraph 6.
fields.PURPOSE: Avoids parallel certification and connects to the existing ENISA framework.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: EUCC · European cybersecurity certification scheme based on the Common Criteria The first scheme adopted under the Cybersecurity Act. It builds on the Common Criteria and the associated evaluation methodology and covers assurance levels substantial and high. ICT products are certified against protection profiles. Relationship to eIDAS: in practice the likely frame of reference for the cybersecurity elements of European Digital Identity Wallet certification under Article 5c(2) eIDAS and of electronic identification scheme certification under Article 12a(2) eIDAS. ● Summary, not verified against the original text Article 12a(2) eIDAS · Link to the Cybersecurity Act Requires that certification be carried out under a relevant cybersecurity certification scheme adopted pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2019/881, or parts thereof, in so far as that scheme covers the requirements.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Which CSA scheme was applied – and does it cover the cybersecurity requirements in full?
fields.KEY POINT: Cyber -> CSA scheme. Non-cyber -> national scheme (paragraph 3).

fields.TOPIC: National certification schemes for the remainder
fields.CONTENT: For requirements that are not relevant for cybersecurity, and for cybersecurity-relevant requirements that are not covered, or only partially covered, by CSA schemes, the Member States (MS) SHALL ESTABLISH national certification schemes following the requirements set out in the implementing act under paragraph 6. Draft schemes are to be transmitted to the Cooperation Group, which MAY issue opinions and recommendations.
fields.PURPOSE: Closes the gap between cybersecurity and the remaining requirements (e.g. usability, data protection architecture).
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5c(6) · Implementing act on European Digital Identity Wallet certification Establishes reference standards, specifications and procedures for certification under paragraphs 1, 2 and 3. Together with Article 5a(23), the second trigger of the 24-month deadline. Without a uniform certification scheme, a European Digital Identity Wallet certificate from one Member State would not be dependable in another – and the list under Article 5d would have no common yardstick. Article 46e eIDAS · European Digital Identity Cooperation Group Establishes the Cooperation Group, in which the Member States coordinate practical application. It facilitates peer review and the exchange of experience and issues opinions and recommendations – inter alia on the draft national European Digital Identity Wallet certification schemes under Article 5c(3) and on the notifications under Article 5d.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Does the national scheme exist – and has it been transmitted to the Cooperation Group?
fields.KEY POINT: Two worlds of certification, one certificate.

fields.TOPIC: Period of validity and vulnerability assessment
fields.ADDRESSEE: Conformity assessment body / provider of the European Digital Identity Wallet
fields.CONTENT: Certification shall be valid for UP TO FIVE YEARS, PROVIDED THAT a vulnerability assessment is carried out EVERY TWO YEARS. Where a vulnerability is identified and NOT remedied IN A TIMELY MANNER, the certification SHALL BE CANCELLED.
fields.PURPOSE: Prevents the 'certificate as a snapshot' – without recurring assessment, any security statement becomes outdated.
fields.DEADLINE: 5 years max. / vulnerability assessment every 2 years
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 12a(3) eIDAS · Five years, two years, three months A more precise variant of the 5/2 rule: certification of an electronic identification scheme is valid for up to five years where a vulnerability assessment is carried out every two years; where a vulnerability is not remedied within three months of being identified, the certification shall be cancelled. At the same point Article 5c(4) says only 'in a timely manner', and Article 30(3a) gives no time limit at all – a popular examination topic. Relevance here: the same 5/2 system, but there with an express three-month time limit instead of the indeterminate 'in a timely manner'. Article 30(3a) eIDAS · Five-year limit for QSCD certifications New in eIDAS 2.0: certification of a qualified electronic signature creation device shall not exceed five years, provided that vulnerability assessments are carried out every two years; where vulnerabilities are not remedied, the certification shall be cancelled. Previously QSCD certificates were in effect open-ended, which was untenable in the face of ageing cryptography.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: When did the last vulnerability assessment take place? Have the findings been demonstrably closed?
fields.KEY POINT: 5 years – 2 years – cancel. The same 5/2 rule applies in 12a(3) and 30(3a).

fields.ADDRESSEE: Provider of the European Digital Identity Wallet
fields.CONTENT: Compliance with the requirements of Article 5a relating to the processing of personal data MAY be certified pursuant to the GDPR.
fields.PURPOSE: A bridge to Article 42 GDPR – voluntary, but strong evidence in supervisory proceedings.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 42 GDPR · Certification Provides for the establishment of data protection certification mechanisms and of data protection seals and marks, for the purpose of demonstrating compliance with that Regulation. Certification is voluntary, limited to a maximum of three years and does not reduce the responsibility of the controller. Relationship to eIDAS: Article 5c(5) eIDAS expressly allows the data protection related requirements of Article 5a to be certified under the GDPR – a may-provision that facilitates the demonstration required by Article 5a(17). ● Summary, not verified against the original text Article 5a(17) · Demonstration of GDPR compliance Requires appropriate and effective data protection measures and expressly requires that compliance of the processing operations with the GDPR BE DEMONSTRATED. This restates, specifically for the European Digital Identity Wallet, the accountability obligation of Article 5(2) GDPR. National provisions further specifying its application remain permissible.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is a GDPR certification used to provide the demonstration required by 5a(17)?

fields.TOPIC: Empowerment to adopt implementing acts – certification
fields.CONTENT: Implementing act containing a list of reference standards and, where necessary, specifications and procedures for the certification referred to in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3.
fields.PURPOSE: Without a uniform certification scheme, a European Digital Identity Wallet certificate from Member State (MS) A would not be dependable in MS B. This act is at the same time the SECOND trigger of the 24-month deadline under Article 5a(1).
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(1) · Obligation to provide and the deadline anchor Establishes the central implementation obligation of Chapter II: every Member State must provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet. The decisive element is the deadline mechanism – the 24 months do not run from the date of the Regulation but from the entry into force of TWO implementing acts: Article 5a(23) (core functionalities) and Article 5c(6) (certification). As long as either one is missing, the period does not begin to run. The same anchor governs Article 5f(2) (36 months) and Article 45e(1). “each Member State shall provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months of the date of entry into force of the implementing acts referred to in paragraph 23 of this Article and in Article 5c(6)” ✓ Article 5a(1) eIDAS Article 5f(2) · Acceptance obligation of certain private entities Covers private relying parties that are required by Union law, national law or contractual obligation to use strong user authentication – the areas mentioned include transport, energy, banking, financial services, social security, health, digital infrastructure, education and telecommunications. Microenterprises and small enterprises are excluded; acceptance takes place only upon the voluntary request of the user. Deadline: 36 months from the same anchor as Article 5a(1). “Where private relying parties that provide services, with the exception of microenterprises and small enterprises” ✓ Article 5f(2) eIDAS Article 45e(1) eIDAS · Verification of attributes against authentic sources Requires the Member States to ensure that, at least for the eleven attributes listed in Annex VI – in so far as they rely on authentic sources within the public sector – electronic verification is possible at the request of the user. Without access to registers, an electronic attestation of attributes would be a mere assertion. Deadline: the same 24-month anchor as Article 5a(1).
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Has the certification implementing act been adopted – and does it cover the certification under paragraphs 1, 2 and 3?
fields.KEY POINT: The clock only starts running once BOTH implementing acts are in force: 5a(23) AND 5c(6).
